goalTextEn: Can use introduction patterns from Lessons 1-4 in a combined scenario.
goalTextKr: 레슨 1~4의 소개 패턴을 조합한 상황에서 사용할 수 있다.

introduce.goalEn: Can use introduction patterns from Lessons 1-4 in a combined scenario.
introduce.goalKr: 레슨 1~4의 소개 패턴을 조합한 상황에서 사용할 수 있다.
introduce.situationEn: Today is a review lesson. You will use everything from Lessons 1-4: greeting people, reading profiles, talking about yourself, and introducing teammates.
introduce.situationKr: 오늘은 복습 레슨입니다. 레슨 1~4에서 배운 모든 것을 사용합니다: 인사, 프로필 읽기, 자기소개, 팀원 소개.

tutorNotes.text: "Today is a review lesson! We'll use everything from Lessons 1 to 4."
Read the lesson goal aloud. Ask the student to repeat.
"This is a chance to practice everything together. Ready?"
Check the student remembers previous lessons. Quick warm-up: 'Can you introduce yourself in 3 sentences?'
Review lessons should feel lighter and more fun. Less teaching, more practicing.

vocabulary.definition: a polite greeting when you meet someone for the first time
a person you work with at the same company
a section of a company (e.g., sales, marketing)
to tell someone your name and information
an activity you enjoy in your free time

pronunciation.instruction: Review: Let's practice all the tricky sounds from Lessons 1-4.
pronunciation.instructionKr: 복습: 레슨 1~4의 어려운 발음을 모두 연습합시다.

tutorNotes.text: "Let's quickly review all the patterns from Lessons 1-4."
Read each pattern. Ask: 'Do you remember this? Which lesson was it from?'
Do a quick vocabulary quiz — say the Japanese, student says the English.
Don't spend too long here. This is warm-up for the practice section.

understand.instruction: Match the pattern to the correct situation. Then complete the fill-in-the-blank review.
understand.instructionKr: 패턴을 올바른 상황에 맞추세요. 그런 다음 빈칸 채우기 복습을 완성하세요.

patternDrills.label: All About Me (L1-L3 Review)
patternDrills.template: I am ___. I am from ___. I work at ___. I like ___.

examples.en: I am Yuki. I am from Sapporo. I work at Global Corp. I like traveling.
examples.kr: 저는 유키입니다. 삿포로 출신입니다. 글로벌코프에서 일하고 있습니다. 여행을 좋아합니다.

patternDrills.label: About Others (L1 & L4 Review)
patternDrills.template: This is ___. He/She is ___. He/She works in ___.

examples.en: This is Kenji. He is our accountant. He works in the finance department.
examples.kr: 이쪽은 켄지입니다. 그는 경리 담당입니다. 그는 경리부에서 일하고 있습니다.

tutorNotes.text: Do the fill-in-the-blank review. This covers ALL patterns from Lessons 1-4.
If the student struggles with a pattern, note which lesson it's from for extra practice.
Use this as a diagnostic — identify weak areas for extra focus later.

steps.title: Step 1 — Quick Recall
steps.instructionEn: Answer each question using a pattern from Lessons 1-4.
steps.instructionKr: 레슨 1~4의 패턴을 사용하여 각 질문에 답하세요.
steps.content:
1. What is your name? → I'm ___.
2. Where are you from? → I am from ___.
3. Where do you work? → I work at ___.
4. What do you like? → I like ___.
5. Who is your manager? → This is ___. He/She is ___.
6. What department are they in? → He/She works in the ___ department.

tutorNotes.text: Ask each question quickly. Student should answer with the correct pattern.
This is a speed drill — encourage quick responses.
If the student answers too slowly on a pattern, mark it for extra practice.

steps.title: Step 2 — Profile Exchange
steps.instructionEn: Read this profile, then introduce this person to your tutor.
steps.instructionKr: 이 프로필을 읽은 다음, 이 사람을 선생님에게 소개하세요.
steps.content:
Profile: Akiko Suzuki
- From: Kobe
- Lives in: Yokohama
- Company: Star Electronics
- Department: Engineering
- Job: Software engineer
- In charge of: Mobile app development
- Hobby: Yoga

Introduce Akiko:
"This is Akiko Suzuki. She is from Kobe. She lives in Yokohama. She works at Star Electronics. She is a software engineer in the engineering department. She is in charge of mobile app development. She likes yoga."

tutorNotes.text: Show the profile. Ask the student to introduce Akiko using the patterns.
First try: student can look at the profile. Second try: cover the profile.
A model answer is provided, but the student's version doesn't need to be identical.

steps.title: Step 3 — Full Networking Dialogue
steps.instructionEn: Practice a complete dialogue. You are at a networking event. Introduce yourself and a colleague.
steps.instructionKr: 완전한 대화를 연습하세요. 네트워킹 이벤트에 있습니다. 자기 자신과 동료를 소개하세요.

dialogue.en: Hi there! I'm Sarah from Blue Wave Inc. What's your name?
dialogue.kr: 안녕하세요! 블루웨이브의 사라입니다. 이름이 어떻게 되세요?

dialogue.en: Nice to meet you! Where are you from?
I am from (hometown). I live in (city) now.
And who is that with you?
This is (colleague name). He/She is our (role). He/She works in the (department) department.
We work together on (project/team). He/She is in charge of (area).
dialogue.kr: 우리는 (프로젝트/팀)에서 함께 일하고 있습니다. 그/그녀는 (분야)를 담당하고 있습니다.

tutorNotes.text: This dialogue uses ALL patterns from Lessons 1-4.
Student fills in with real or imagined information.
First run: read along. Second run: try from memory.
Pay attention to which patterns the student uses confidently vs. struggles with.

steps.title: Step 4 — Presentation: Your Team
steps.instructionEn: Give a short presentation (1-2 minutes). Introduce yourself and your team to the class.
steps.instructionKr: 짧은 프레젠테이션 (1~2분)을 해 봅시다. 반에 자기 자신과 팀을 소개하세요.
steps.content:
Your presentation should include:
1. Introduce yourself (name, hometown, company, hobby)
2. Introduce 2-3 team members (name, role, department, responsibility)
3. Describe your team (we work together in...)

Example:
"Hello! My name is Yuki. I am from Sapporo. I work at Global Corp.
This is Kenji. He is our accountant. He works in the finance department.
This is Maria. She is a sales assistant. She is in charge of our online store.
We work together in the Tokyo office. Nice to meet you all!"

tutorNotes.text: "For the final practice, give me a short presentation about yourself and your team."
Give the student 1-2 minutes to prepare, then present.
Score: Check if they can use patterns from ALL 4 lessons.
This is the key assessment for the review. Note strengths and weaknesses.

challenge.scenarioEn: You are the MC at a company welcome party. A new employee and a visiting client have just arrived. Introduce yourself, introduce 3 team members to them, and answer their questions.
challenge.scenarioKr: 회사 환영회의 사회를 보고 있습니다. 신입사원과 방문 고객이 도착했습니다. 자기소개를 하고 팀원 3명을 소개하고 질문에 답하세요.

guideQuestions.text: Greet the guests and introduce yourself.
Introduce at least 3 team members with names, roles, and departments.

tutorNotes.text: "OK, the final challenge! You're the MC at a welcome party. I'll play the new employee AND the client. Ready?"
As new employee: 'Hi! I'm Tomoko. I just joined. Can you introduce the team?'
As client: 'Hello! I'm Robert from ABC Inc. Nice to meet you. Tell me about your team.'
Grade: Can the student comfortably combine self-intro + team introductions? Do they use all the key patterns?
This is the final assessment for Lessons 1-4. If the student does well, they're ready for Chapter 2!

discussion.instructionEn: Choose one category, then answer the questions. Use the patterns from Lessons 1-4.
discussion.instructionKr: 카테고리를 하나 선택하고 질문에 답하세요. 레슨 1~4의 패턴을 사용하세요.

categories.title: LOOKING BACK
questions: Which pattern do you use the most?
What was the most difficult vocabulary word?

categories.title: COMPANY EVENTS
questions: Does your company have welcome parties?
Have you ever been an MC?

categories.title: FIRST IMPRESSIONS
questions: What makes a good first impression?
What do you notice first when meeting someone?

tutorNotes.text: "Let's have a final discussion before we wrap up."
Ask the student to choose a category.
Use this time to identify if the student needs to revisit any lesson before Chapter 2.

tutorNotes.text: "Congratulations! You've completed all 5 lessons in Chapter 1!"
Ask the student to read the lesson goal.
"Were you able to achieve today's lesson goal?"
Fill in the detailed feedback template. Note which lessons need review.
Practice mispronounced words.
"Next chapter is about the office — office supplies, rooms, and directions. See you soon!"
If the student struggled, suggest reviewing specific lessons before moving on.
